svg.title: Yomika tray mark
svg.desc: The brand mark re-derived for the Windows notification area. Same rounded plate and same two-tier ink as `yomika-mark-print.svg`, but the glyph is filled instead of stroked and reduced from five elements to three: at the 16px the tray actually gives it, the print mark's 18-unit strokes land on 0.56px and the whole thing dissolves into grey mush (user report: "在小尺寸下很难看清"). Every edge here sits on a 32-unit boundary, so a 512-unit master downsamples 1:2 to the 32px tray bitmap and 1:32 to a 16px render on exact pixel boundaries — the 128-unit stroke is a full 4px, the dot 5px across. The accent frame is dropped, not forgotten: at 16px it stole the width the glyph needs (candidate "C-framed" in the tray-icon study), and the plate already carries the identity.
